_about: Known behaviour of a shared part that controls and the device matrix must respect, keyed by devices.json traits (selectors: docs/DEVICES.md, Traits), so a quirk found on one handheld covers every sibling with the same part. applies: selector. what: one line. why: the shared part. used_by: the code that reads it (Traits.has_quirk). Report: python3 tools/traits/traits.py model <id>.

quirks.what: The firmware accepts SPPT / FPPT writes and ignores them; RAPL (PowerStation) is the real limit.
quirks.why: MSI's Panther Lake Claw firmware (msi-wmi-platform ppt_* attributes); measured on the Claw 8 EX.

quirks.what: thermald puts the firmware's power limits back every few seconds, so Power holds it while GameCove sets a lower TDP (with a temperature guard).
quirks.why: Every Intel handheld runs Intel's thermald on Bazzite.

quirks.what: gamescope ships a display script for this panel and switches its refresh rate itself.
quirks.why: The panel's EDID matches one of gamescope's known displays (traits.panel.gamescope).

quirks.what: gamescope-session-plus sets CUSTOM_REFRESH_RATES for this handheld, so gamescope switches refresh already.
quirks.why: The device-quirks blocks for the ONEXPLAYER X1 A / X1 i / X1 mini and G1 (the X1 Pro has none).

quirks.what: gamescope drives this OLED in HDR10 and the backlight does nothing; brightness is gamescope's SDR-on-HDR level.
While gamescope outputs PQ (HDR) the backlight is ignored, so brightness is the SDR-on-HDR level, re-applied after suspend.
quirks.why: Samsung AMS881KB01-0 OLED, driven over eDP AUX luminance in PQ (both Legion Go 2 SoC models).

quirks.what: Switching HDR on or off at runtime can leave the screen off until a long power press or a second reboot.
quirks.reason: Switching HDR can turn this screen off until a reboot

quirks.what: Fan and charge behaviour come from the oxpec EC driver (hwmon oxp_ec); the Orange Pi Neo shares it with OneXPlayer and AOKZOE.
quirks.why: The Linux oxpec driver's DMI table lists OneXPlayer, AOKZOE and the Orange Pi Neo (NEO-01).

quirks.what: The volume buttons are keys on the i8042 keyboard, a wakeup source (fix claw-kbd-wakeup).
quirks.why: Every MSI Claw board (InputPlumber lists the AT keyboard as a source on all of them).

quirks.what: Linux's panel orientation quirk matches board G0A1W only; G1A1W units would start sideways, so GameCove's session sets ORIENTATION=left on G1A1W (session_quirk zotac-g1a1w-left).
quirks.why: drm_panel_orientation_quirks.c ZOTAC Gaming Zone entry: DMI_EXACT_MATCH board G0A1W, lcd1080x1920_leftside_up (checked on master, 2026-11-09). InputPlumber's 50-zotac-zone.yaml and its autostart hwdb list both G0A1W and G1A1W; gamescope-session-plus's device-quirks has no Zone block.
quirks.used_by: session/gamescope-session-plus/sessions.d/gamecove (ORIENTATION, only when unset); display.rotation can still change it
